{{Short description|Danish statistician (1878–1939)}}
'''Kirstine Smith''' (April 12, 1878 – November 11, 1939) was a Danish [[statistician]]. She is credited with the creation of the field of [[Optimal design|optimal design of experiments]].

==Background==

Smith grew up in the town of [[Nykøbing Mors]], [[Denmark]]. In 1903, she graduated from the [[University of Copenhagen]] with a degree in mathematics and physics. After, she worked as secretary to astronomer and statistician [[Thorvald Nicolai Thiele|Thorvald Thiele]]<ref name="gump">[http://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~gumpertz/  Gumpertz, M.L. Thumbnail biography of Kirstine Smith (Accessed 23 August 2013).]</ref> and later with the [[International Council for the Exploration of the Sea]] for which she authored several volumes on fish populations.<ref name="crary">[http://www.webdoe.cc/publications/kirstine.php Crary Group (Accessed 23 August 2013 via Google archive).] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090810040534/http://www.webdoe.cc/publications/kirstine.php |date=10 August 2009 }}</ref>

In 1916, Smith was admitted for doctoral training at the [[University of London]] where [[Karl Pearson]] had founded the first university statistics department. She was a student of Pearson who described her as "brilliant" in a letter to [[Ronald Aylmer Fisher|Ronald Fisher]].<ref name=GL2009>{{cite journal |last1=Guttorp |first1=P. |last2=Lindgren |first2=G. |title= Karl Pearson and the Scandinavian school of statistics |journal= International Statistical Review |volume=77 |year=2009 |page=64 |doi=10.1111/j.1751-5823.2009.00069.x|s2cid=121294724 }}</ref> At London, she produced an influential paper in the journal ''[[Biometrika]]'' on [[minimum chi-square estimation]] of the correlation coefficient.<ref name="GL2009"/> Disagreements about aspects of her work led to increased friction between Pearson and Fisher.<ref name="GL2009"/>

In her dissertation, which was published in 1918 (see below), she invented [[optimal design]] where she computed G-optimal designs for [[polynomial regression]] of order up to 6.<ref name="GL2009"/> After finishing her doctorate she moved to [[Copenhagen]], where she worked as a researcher for the Commission for Ocean Research 1918 to 1924 and with [[Johannes Schmidt (biologist)|Johannes Schmidt]] at the [[Carlsberg Laboratory]] from 1920 to 1921.<ref name="gump"/> She eventually left research after obtaining her teaching credentials to become a high school teacher.<ref name="crary"/>

==Selected statistical papers==

*Smith, K. (1916). On the 'best' values of the constants in frequency distributions. ''Biometrika'', ''11''(3), 262–276.
*Smith, K. (1918). On the standard deviations of adjusted and interpolated values of an observed polynomial function and its constants and the guidance they give towards a proper choice of the distribution of observations. ''Biometrika'', ''12''(1/2), 1–85.
*Smith, K. (1922).The standard deviations of fraternal and parental correlation coefficients. ''Biometrika'', ''14''(1/2), 1–22.
